title: Chainflip says attacker took BTC, ETH and stablecoins from its vaults; offers 10% bounty
date_note: Chainflip's message says the funds were taken on 21 November 2026; the Part 1 incident report timeline gives 06:41:01 UTC for the first theft (BTC) and 07:10:59 UTC for the Ethereum vault.
geo_basis: No page read states where Chainflip is based or where the affected systems are.
summary: Chainflip Labs said in a message to the attacker that on 21 November 2026 they took 122.86137042 BTC, 520.2243399 ETH, 3,249,631.41 USDC and 758,141.33 USDT from its vaults, and offered a 10% bounty. Its Part 2 incident report (27 November) says the attacker exploited a use-after-free flaw in libzmq to run code inside validator processes, and that the protocol remains paused.
plain: The crypto service Chainflip says an attacker took bitcoin, ether and stablecoins from its vaults on 21 November. It offers to let the attacker keep 10% if 90% is returned by 23 November.
exec: Chainflip says funds were taken from its vaults; its Part 2 report says a libzmq flaw in validator software was exploited and the protocol remains paused.
impact: Funds taken from Chainflip vaults; swaps, deposits and withdrawals paused in safe mode according to Chainflip incident report. CryptoSlate reports the report says Chainflip began precautionary returns of free liquidity-provider balances on Solana, Arbitrum, Tron, BNB Chain and Polkadot Asset Hub, without a compensation timetable. Part 2 report says a protocol-managed user recovery fund can be implemented once accounting is on-chain.

validation.note: Primary: Chainflip Labs' own message to the attacker (chainflip.io/return) states the amounts, bounty and deadline. CryptoTicker and Shattered independently report the drain and safe mode. Chainflip's incident report (Part 1, 23 November) also states the further 10.48288011 BTC; total value in USD varies by outlet (about $12 million per Cointelegraph, relayed by CryptoTicker) and is left out.
